findings.what_viewer_sees: In gag 10a the Explorer runs sideways across the tiny planet, but his legs strafe the opposite way to his travel (a moonwalk). The grounded foot slides along with the body instead of planting, so the whole run looks like ice-skating.
findings.evidence: FK of models/adventurer.glb (script review6/s10work/glb/fk.py). Run_Left planted feet move -3.0 model units/s in x, so the clip travels +x: the character's left, which is screen-right for this camera-facing hero. Run_Right is the mirror (+3.0). The code moves him to screen-left (x 0 to -1.05) while playing Run_Left, and to screen-right (-1.05 to +1.0) while playing Run_Right. In /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/runL28024_8x1_c.jpg the grounded right foot travels left with the body over 28028-28031 instead of staying put; runfeet28060_12x1_c.jpg shows the same in reverse.
findings.likely_cause: The strafe clips are assigned by screen direction, but Quaternius Run_Left/Run_Right are named from the character's point of view, and he faces the camera (ry=0). There is also a speed mismatch: the clip's natural speed is about 1.65 world u/s at scale 0.55, while the Run_Right path peaks at about 3.4 u/s (2.05 u in 0.95 s, inOutSine).
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:442 (hero.play timeline) and ch6.js:447-450 (heroX run segments)
findings.suggested_fix: Swap the clips: hero.play(runL0, 'Run_Right', ...)... .play(runR0, 'Run_Left', ...). Then match speed: for the second run use a near-linear path (short ease in/out) and/or { speed: ~1.6 } on the clip, or lengthen runR1-runR0 to about 1.3 s, so the planted foot stays still relative to the planet.

findings.what_viewer_sees: After the second run the Explorer stands in Idle and glides back toward centre by about 150-200 px over 1.3 s with his feet still. He straightens up from his lean while drifting, as if on a conveyor, and the comment bubble drifts with him.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/glideB28098_12x4_c.jpg: the hero is at about x=1305 at 28098 and about x=1100 at 28134 in the idle pose, with no steps.
findings.likely_cause: heroX lerps 1.0 to 0.35 between runR1+0.3 and runR1+1.6 while the clip timeline plays 'Idle' from runR1, so root translation has no locomotion.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:451 (return lerp(1.0, 0.35, prog(t, runR1 + 0.3, runR1 + 1.6, E.inOutSine))) with ch6.js:442
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the root where the run ended (return 1.0) and re-centre by easing the camera target/look instead, or schedule a locomotion clip for the drift. For example, hero.play(runR1 + 0.25, 'Run_Right' (screen-left for him) or a 'Walk' turned with ry toward -x, {speed ≈ 0.7}) and then 'Idle' at runR1 + 1.6, so the feet plant.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Three transitions blink to black: gag 10a to the splash map, the splash map to the heat globe, and the drip globe to the Bacon desk. A full-brightness picture is replaced by a black frame, and the new shot then fades up over about 0.3 s. There is no fade-out, so it reads as a dropout or blink rather than a crossfade.
findings.evidence: Mean luminance per frame: 25.1 -> 2.1 at 28137, then a linear ramp to 17.3 at 28146. Likewise 23.5 -> 1.8 at 28317 (ramp to 28326) and 16.5 -> 2.2 at 28891 (ramp to 28898). Detector events E13, E17 and E25 show pure-black event frames; E14 is the end of the first ramp.
findings.likely_cause: These base scenes are declared with { fadeIn: 0.3 / 0.3 / 0.25 }. film.html blends a fadeIn scene over whatever is below it (alpha = lt/fadeIn, so 0 on the first frame). But each outgoing base scene ends exactly at the incoming t0 (gag 10a ends at GA1 = SP0, splash at SP1 = HT0, drip globe at D1 = BC0), so the fade happens over the black safety-net background. ENGINE.md says to keep the outgoing scene running until the incoming fade ends.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:481 (base(GA0, GA1)), ch6.js:532 (base(SP0, SP1)), ch6.js:664 (base(D0, D1)); fadeIn at ch6.js:555, 591, 704
findings.suggested_fix: Overlap the outgoing scenes by the fade length: base(GA0, GA1 + 0.3, ...), base(SP0, SP1 + 0.3, ...), base(D0, D1 + 0.25, ...). None of the pairs share globe or overlay state: 3D stage to 2D, 2D to fut.draw, globe to 2D. Alternatively drop the three fadeIn options for clean cuts.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'shot.', when the blank film frame turns live, the whole filmstrip snaps about 6% smaller in one frame. The scroll also stops dead from 22 px/frame. The push-in then restarts from scratch and creeps for about 0.4 s before whooshing into the hole, so the beat reads as a hiccup instead of one continuous push.
findings.evidence: Sprocket pitch is 74 px in 29458-29463 and 70 px from 29464. The top sprocket row moves from y 310-332 to 322-343 and the bottom from 747-769 to 736-757. Horizontal shift is -22 px/frame up to 29463 and 0 from 29464 to 29465. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/snapzoom29462_4x1.jpg. Detector E32 (motion_stop at 29465) marks the same moment.
findings.likely_cause: The pre-live zoom ends at 1 + 0.06 = 1.06, but the live branch restarts at lerp(1, ..., inExpo(0)) = 1.0. tt = min(t, M.shot - 0.05) also freezes a linear scroll (V2*(M.frame - tt)) with no deceleration.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the live zoom where the pre-live one ends: lerp(1.06, W / FW * 1.1, prog(t, M.shot - 0.05, M.shot + 0.7, inExpo)). Make BLANK_I arrive centred and at rest at TF = M.shot - 0.05: V2 = (BLANK_I - TODAY_I) * PITCH / (TF - M.frame), and replace the linear scroll term with a curve that decelerates to zero over the last ~0.6 s (quadratic ease-out, distance preserved).

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the switch from s097 (bus in the gap) to s098 (pull-back), the cyan Mid-Atlantic Ridge line jumps from faint to full brightness in one frame, then fades out over 0.5 s. In the same frame the faint orange continent tint and drip arcs disappear.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/sw26474_6x1.jpg: the ridge is clearly brighter in 26477 than in 26476. The frame-diff spike is 4.70 against about 1.7 around it, and the detector missed it.
findings.likely_cause: s097 draws the ridge at alpha 1 - 0.4*prog(...) = 0.6 by A1. s098 draws drawRidge(ctx, t, fa) with fa starting at 1. s098's globe() also passes ovAlpha 0 and overlay null (s097 had COLD at 0.12) and does not continue the 0.18-alpha drip arcs. The camera also changes from moving to starting at rest (alt about 0.914 to 0.9).
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:322 and ch6.js:325 (s098 base) vs ch6.js:286-288 (s097)
findings.suggested_fix: In s098 use drawRidge(ctx, t, 0.6 * fa). Keep the overlay fading: globe(ctx, camB(t), {..., ovAlpha: 0.12 * fa}, fa > 0 ? COLD : null). Add drawArcs(ctx, t, 0, { full: true, alpha: 0.18 * fa }) while fa > 0.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'supercontinent will form' globe spin turns 24-38° per frame at its peak. Each frame shows a different face of the Earth (Asia, India, Middle East, Europe/Africa, Atlantic, North America, Pacific within 10 frames), so at speed it strobes and flickers rather than reading as a spin.
findings.likely_cause: The longitude term rotates 750° over SPIN1-SPIN0 = 1.9 s with a cubic inOut, and there is no motion blur.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut to about 300-360° (peak ≤ 15°/frame), lengthen the spin, or add a cheap sub-frame blur during the spin (average 3-4 globe renders at sub-times, or stronger fog earlier).

findings.what_viewer_sees: Audio, not picture: right after 'Amasia.' a short breath or mouth noise starts and is chopped off, which can be heard as a small click.
findings.evidence: In audio/vo/vo_proc.wav the voice is silent (-84 dB) at 919.84 after the word, then a 70 ms burst rises to -27 dB (919.86-919.92) and is cut to -88 dB by 919.94. In the final mix the level drops from -24 to -35 dB at 919.93. This matches the README audio flag at 15:19.92.
findings.likely_cause: Each TTS take is trimmed at last-char end + 90 ms and gets only an 8 ms fade-out, so a breath that starts inside the 90 ms margin is cut mid-sound.
findings.code_location: tools/tts.py:99 (b = en[last] + 0.09) and tools/tts.py:102 (8 ms fade)
findings.suggested_fix: Keep clip lengths, so timing does not change, but fade the tail to silence from last-char end + 10 ms over 30-40 ms (or end at the RMS minimum inside the margin). For s101 only, a 40 ms VO-track fade starting at 919.86 in the mix also works.

findings.what_viewer_sees: As the Aurica tile finishes expanding to full screen, Australia's gold glow switches off in one frame. It returns about 4 s later on 'middle'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/aurglow27625_6x1_c.jpg. Australia region mean RGB goes 72/61/48 -> 60/51/45 and yellow-pixel share 0.067 -> 0.011 at 27628. Frame diff is 0.50 against 0.1. The other three tile-to-live handovers (26808, 27097, 27384) are seamless.
findings.likely_cause: The tile still S[3].a is drawn with drawLive(..., still=true), and MODELS[3].extra uses a = 0.5 when still. The first live frame at tLive uses a = prog(t, M.middle - 0.1, ...) = 0.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch6.js:189 (const a = still ? 0.5 : prog(...)); still built at ch6.js:203
findings.suggested_fix: Use the time-based alpha in both cases, so the still matches the first live frame: const a = prog(t, M.middle - 0.1, M.middle + 0.25). Let `still` suppress only the yRing.

findings.what_viewer_sees: During the 'UNDER 1 IN 10 -> 6' countdown, the whole line jumps about 25 px sideways when 10 becomes 9.
findings.evidence: Text extent is x 1212..1747 at 28465 and 1237..1722 at 28466; widths stay equal for 9/8/7/6. See num28462_16x1_c.jpg in review6/grab_s10.
findings.likely_cause: The string 'UNDER 1 IN ' + n is drawn with align 'center', so the line re-centres when the number loses a digit.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor it to the widest string: x0 = x - F.measure(ctx, 'UNDER 1 IN 10', fo) / 2, then draw with align 'left' at x0, or draw the static words and the number with separate fixed anchors.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The four tiles settle into the filmstrip, ending with a slight rightward drift, then come to rest. On the next frame the strip is already scrolling left at full speed, a visible hitch with a direction reversal.
findings.evidence: Cross-correlation shift per frame: +2, +9, +4, +2, +1, 0 (28691-28696), then -3 (28697), then a constant -13 px/frame from 28698. Detector E23 marks this motion_start.
findings.likely_cause: The scroll is a linear term -V1*max(0, t - (M.wins + 0.55)) that starts at full speed the moment the inOutExpo morph ends.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace max(0, u) with an eased ramp, e.g. ramp = u => u <= 0 ? 0 : u < 0.4 ? u*u/0.8 : u - 0.2, and start it slightly earlier (M.wins + 0.4) so it accelerates under the tail of the morph.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'one frame of a very slow movie' the strip of map frames pans at about 666 px/s (22 px per frame). The high-contrast sprocket holes and globes judder or strobe at 30 fps, and the highlighted TODAY frame slides off within about 1.5 s.
findings.evidence: Measured a constant -22 px/frame for 29401-29409 by cross-correlation, and sprocket-row offsets of -22/-23 px per frame at 29459-29463. Sprocket pitch is 70-74 px, so each step is about 1/3 pitch.
findings.likely_cause: V2 = 5 frames * 690 px / (M.shot - M.frame = 5.18 s) is about 666 px/s, well above the speed at which a 30p pan of fine detail looks smooth.
findings.suggested_fix: Lower the pan speed: put the blank frame 3-4 frames after TODAY instead of 5, or reduce PITCH while sZ = 1. Alternatively soften the sprocket pattern during the scroll (lower alpha or a 2-3 px horizontal smear).

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the end of the zoom into the live frame, a white vertical line (the hole's border) flashes at the left edge of the screen for 2 frames, then vanishes at the cut to the Afar scene.
findings.evidence: In the left 80 px the brightest column is 88 at x=33 (29486) and 82.7 at x=12 (29487), against a median of about 1.5; it drops to 2.2 at 29488. See leftedge29484_5x1_c.jpg in review6/grab_s10.
findings.likely_cause: The hole is centred at fxB = fX(9, M.shot - 0.05) ≈ 993 px rather than 960 because of the early freeze. The final zoom W/FW*1.02 (≈3.26) only just exceeds the frame width, so the 3*zoom px border strokeRect sits on the left edge until FS1.
findings.suggested_fix: With the S10-4 fix the hole is centred. Also raise the end zoom to about W/FW*1.1, or fade the border with ctx.globalAlpha = 0.5 * (1 - prog(zoom, 1.6, 2.6)).

findings.what_viewer_sees: The glowing sparks along the three Afar rift arms all pop on at full brightness in one frame. They then hop forward in jumps of about 25-35 px roughly every 6 frames, ticking along rather than flowing, for the rest of the film including the end screen.
findings.evidence: Spark peaks on the Gulf of Aden arm: x 1151/1293/1493 for 29640-29645, 1166/1316/1528 for 29646-29651, then 1191/1348/1563 from 29652. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s10/sparkstep29643_12x1_c.jpg; the pop-in is visible at 29568 in t29502_24x3.jpg.
findings.likely_cause: Each spark uses q = P[floor(u*(P.length-1))] with no interpolation between densified points, so a ~25-point arm gives one step every ~0.23 s. All sparks start at full alpha when cp >= 1, and u % 1 makes them teleport from the arm end back to the junction.
findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate: f = u*(P.length-1), i0 = floor(f), i1 = min(i0+1, P.length-1), q = lerp(P[i0], P[i1], f - i0). Scale spark alpha by prog(t, M.cracks + 0.9, M.cracks + 1.3) * Math.sin(Math.PI * u) so they fade in and never visibly wrap.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reads fine:
- E1: chapter cut, with the card fading in over the bright globe.
- E2: hard cut to the 4-tile grid on 'four main models'. The '?' marks don't carry over exactly, which is acceptable.
- E3-E11: tile expand and shrink snap zooms (inOutExpo 0.5-0.55 s, consistent across all four models). Tile-to-live handovers at 26808, 27097 and 27384 are seamless; the only exception is the Aurica glow (S10-8).
- E12: gag start.
- E15/E16: the 0.58 s Tuesday-card callback flash.
- E18/E26: counter rolls, landing just before 'sixth' and 'ago'.
- E19, E20, E27, E28, E29: hard cuts on sentence starts.
- E21/E22: grid-to-strip shuffle; tiles 1 and 2 briefly cross, acceptable.
- E24: torn halves exit.
- E30: Gondwana snap.

Defective events:
- E13, E14, E17, E25: S10-3.
- E23: S10-10.
- E32: S10-4.
- Missed by the detectors: S10-1, S10-2, S10-5, S10-6, S10-8, S10-11, S10-12, S10-13.

Chunk starts 26550, 27000, 27450, 27900, 28350, 28800, 29250, 29700 and 30150 show no look change. 29700 and 30150 carry only codec GOP noise: mean |d| 1.2/0.9 in the source chunk files, no shift, gain or offset, R² ≈ 0. In code, globe() resets every uniform fut.draw touches, and the STILLS/HOLD/HEATHOLD/AFHOLD/PSTILLS caches are deterministic, so nothing like the 5:45 needsUpdate bug exists in ch6.

Clean stretches:
- s097 ridge draw, 1620 pill (rides off-frame with the camera as a world pin) and bus drop.
- Proxima, Novopangaea, Amasia and Aurica plate motion, arrows, impacts and holds.
- AU+RICA label assembly.
- Splash convergence.
- Heat build.
- Gag 10b faint: the Death clip lands on 'Reminder', with no T-pose or snapping.
- Tear, drip globe and fingerprint arcs.
- Bacon counter, capes globe, p.246 underlines and gold.
- Gondwana snap with the waving Explorer and porch light.
- Afar fly-in and crack draw-on.
- End screen. The last frame (30328) is live, not black.

Narration sync is within about 0.3 s throughout. The QC 'static' stretches 944.4-948.5 and 958.7-963.0 carry the heat build, a slow zoom and the tip highlights, so they are acceptable holds.
